title: RTL-Breaker: Assessing the Security of LLMs Against Backdoor Attacks on HDL Code Generation
problem: LLM-based HDL code generators are vulnerable to data-poisoning/backdoor attacks; malicious code injected into training data is replicated into generated hardware designs, compromising entire systems.
motivation: LLM adoption in hardware design is growing; data poisoning is realistic given reliance on public repositories for training; hardware backdoors are difficult to detect and can persist through manufacturing.
method: The RTL-Breaker framework tests how to poison LLMs that generate hardware designs (HDL/RTL code specifies how chips operate). It hides malicious patterns in training data to make the LLM produce harmful code in hardware designs, then measures which patterns are most effective and whether the poisoned code still works. It also examines whether attacks stay effective over time. The framework and datasets were released publicly.
key_novelty: This is the first systematic study of how LLMs that generate hardware designs can be poisoned by introducing malicious patterns into training data, examining which patterns work best and whether such poisoning can be detected.
contributions: Novel backdoor attack framework for LLM HDL generation (RTL-Breaker)
Analysis of trigger mechanisms and effectiveness
Assessment of side-effects on code generation quality
Open-source framework and datasets for future research
limitations: Defense mechanisms not proposed; applicability to other LLM code generation tasks (e.g., testbenches, verification) not explored.
primary_theme: LLM backdoor attacks on hardware code generation
